strata0213-fnb-gsq-iq3s-128k.note: A 3-bit quant rechecked on the daily-driver setup (MTP draft head, one 3090 at 300 W, Qwen thinking sampling), with only the weights changed from the UD-Q2_0 runs, to see whether more bits buy quality. Agent test 1 (2026-11-10, OpenCode): every live check passes, 20 subcommands, 255 of its own tests pass, 48 minutes at 117.2 tok/s agent-run decode, first token median 0.31 s; 2.2 GiB free. Test 2: builds, 11 tools, the tool call works and 160 of its own tests pass (64 minutes, 118.0 tok/s, first token median 0.57 s), but it answers an initialize request for the 2024-11-05 protocol version with an error instead of offering a version it supports, so older clients cannot connect. The labyrinth (test 7) scores 8 of 10 at 118.0 tok/s (first token median 0.42 s): one fixed serpentine route for every seed. It is about 14% slower than UD-Q2_0 on every test and does not beat it on any.

strata0213-fnb-gsq-iq3xxs-128k.label: Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS · Strata 0.2.13, RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
strata0213-fnb-gsq-iq3xxs-128k.note: The smaller 3-bit GSQ quant on the daily-driver setup (MTP draft head, one 3090 at 300 W, Qwen thinking sampling), with only the weights changed from the UD-Q2_0 runs. Agent test 1 (2026-11-10, OpenCode): every live check passes, 18 subcommands, 263 of its own tests pass, 65 minutes at 128.9 tok/s agent-run decode, first token median 0.41 s; 2.2 GiB free. Test 2: builds, 9 tools, the 2024-11-05 handshake and the tool call work, 145 of its own tests pass (50 minutes, 134.3 tok/s, first token median 0.38 s). Faster than IQ3_S and close to UD-Q2_0, but fewer tools and tests than UD-Q2_0. The labyrinth (test 7) scored 8 of 10 at 129.2 tok/s (first token median 0.42 s): the route changes with each seed, but it is a comb of one-cell dead ends.

tf127-qwen3.8-27b-exl3-3bpw-dflash2.label: Qwen3.8-27B EXL3 3-bit · TensorFold 1.2.7, DFlash2 drafts, RTX 3090, 128k to 176k, 8-bit cache
tf127-qwen3.8-27b-exl3-3bpw-dflash2.note: The TensorFold 1.2.7 release archive, unchanged, on one 3090 at 300 W with an 8-bit (fp8) K/V cache. Short-benchmark rates. Drafted decode 79 to 87 tok/s on prose, 210 to 217 on code and 204 to 259 on JSON, first token 0.06 to 0.19 s on short prompts; 30k, 128k and 176k retrieval all correct (first token 41 s, 249 s and 388 s). Drafting is lossless here: all 15 fixed prompts give the same text with and without drafting, greedy and sampled, at 2.7 to 7.8 times the plain speed. Quality check 3 of 3. 3.6 GiB free at 176k, so it fits.

tf127-nemotron3.5-lightning-nvfp4.label: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B NVFP4 · TensorFold 1.2.7 (RTX 30 fallback path), RTX 3090, 32k
tf127-nemotron3.5-lightning-nvfp4.note: NVFP4 weights on a 3090, which has no FP4 hardware, through TensorFold's fallback path; it drafts with the export's own MTP head. Short-benchmark rates: 152 to 157 tok/s on prose and 181 to 194 on code, first token 0.04 s on short prompts; 30k retrieval correct with a 4.8 s first token (about 6,300 tok/s prefill). Quality check 1 of 3 (the code task passes; one wrong total and one answer in the wrong format), and we have no same-prompt run on another card to tell model from fallback arithmetic. 3.7 GiB free, fits.

lcpp-arete27b-q8.label: Arete-27B Q8_0 · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), V100 alone, 128k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-arete27b-q8.note: The 8-bit quant of the Nous Research fine-tune, on the V100 alone. Serving tuning only (short-benchmark rates): 23.1 tok/s decode against 26.2 for Q6_K; 128k is the largest context that fits (a 120k retrieval correct, 0.9 GiB free). No agent tests yet.

lcpp-qwen38-27b-udq4km-3090.label: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M (Unsloth, September 2026 file) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090, 96k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-qwen38-27b-udq4km-3090.note: The control for the Unsloth Dynamic V3.1 re-upload: the older file on the 3090 alone at 250 W. Short-benchmark rates: 32.1 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 0.23-0.61 s, 30k and 90k retrievals correct, quality check 3 of 3, 5.4 GiB free. Agent test 1 with thinking on (agent run): passes all five checks with 94 tests passing, 8 subcommands, 68 minutes, engine decode 23.5 tok/s, median first token 0.38 s.

lcpp-qwen38-27b-v31-udq4km-3090.label: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M (Unsloth Dynamic V3.1) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090, 96k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-qwen38-27b-v31-udq4km-3090.note: Unsloth re-uploaded its Qwen3.8-27B quants as Dynamic V3.1 and claims 5-10% better agentic scores. Same flags as the old file, only the file changes. Short-benchmark rates: 32.3 tok/s decode (old file 32.1), short-prompt first token 0.21-0.61 s, 30k and 90k retrievals correct, quality check 3 of 3, 5.3 GiB free (94 MiB less than the old file). Agent test 1 with thinking on (agent run): passes all five checks with 58 tests passing, 7 subcommands, 57 minutes, engine decode 23.9 tok/s, median first token 0.41 s. lcpp-twil8b-balanced-q4km-3090.label: TwIL-8B balanced Q4_K_M (webAI official) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-twil8b-balanced-q4km-3090.note: webAI's new 8B reasoning model (a Granite 4.2-8B post-train, webAI non-commercial licence), on the 3090 alone at its native 128k context with thinking on. Short-benchmark rates: 96.4 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 0.04-0.08 s, 30k and 120k retrievals correct (first token 13.9 s and 122.3 s), 7.6 GiB free. The quality check scored 0 of 3 at our usual token caps because every answer was still thinking when the cap hit; with a 16k cap it scores 3 of 3, using up to 5k tokens of thinking on a short Python task. No agent tests yet.

lcpp-twil8b-verbose-q8-3090.label: TwIL-8B verbose Q8_0 (webAI official) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-twil8b-verbose-q8-3090.note: The verbose variant of TwIL-8B, the largest official quant that fits the 3090 with 128k of 8-bit K/V. Short-benchmark rates: 72.6 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 0.04-0.08 s, 30k retrieval correct; at 120k it found both markers but wrote them with their names attached, which our strict check scores as a miss. 4.1 GiB free. With a 16k token cap the quality check scores 1 of 3: it thought past 16k tokens on a short Python task without answering and got the JSON task wrong. It thinks longer than the balanced variant and scores lower. No agent tests yet.

lcpp-nex-n26-q2k-3090-v100.label: Nex-N2.6 Q2_K (bartowski) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, experts in RAM, 96k, 8-bit KV
lcpp-nex-n26-q2k-3090-v100.note: nex-agi's agent-focused post-train of GLM-5.3-Flash (Apache-2.0), across both cards with llama.cpp placing the experts itself and the rest in system RAM. Short-benchmark rates: 10.6 tok/s decode, short-prompt first token 15-24 s, 30k and 90k retrievals correct but slow (first token 621 s and 1,640 s, about 50 tok/s prefill), quality check 3 of 3, 2.8 GiB free on the 3090 and 3.0 GiB on the V100. Correct and it fits, but a 30k agent prompt would wait about 10 minutes, so no agent tests at this size and placement.

rustingstrata121-fnb-v31-udq2kxl-3090.label: Flash-Next UD-Q2_K_XL (Unsloth Dynamic v3.1) · RustingStrata 1.2.1, RTX 3090, 128k, 8-bit KV
rustingstrata121-fnb-v31-udq2kxl-3090.note: RustingStrata is a new pure-Rust engine for Qwen GGUF files (experts that miss VRAM run on the CPU). Same file, card and 300 W as our Strata 0.2.13 daily-driver control, thinking off, greedy. Short-benchmark, client-side rates (the engine reports no server timings): 34.7 tok/s decode without drafting and 36.7 with its one-token MTP draft, against 120.7 for Strata 0.2.13 on the same file; 30k and 120k retrievals correct (first token about 30 s and 136 s), 2.2 GiB free. A working engine, about 3.5 times slower than Strata.

lcpp-cybertiel35b-abl-q6kxl-3090-v100.label: Cyber-Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B UD-Q6_K_XL (abliterated) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots, 8-bit KV
lcpp-cybertiel35b-abl-q6kxl-3090-v100.note: An abliterated (refusal-removed, uncensored) Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B, tested as a candidate agent backend serving four ~250k sessions at once on both cards, with the same settings as Tiel-Coder for a direct pair. Short-benchmark rates: 107.5 tok/s decode on short prompts, first token 0.37-1.30 s, 250k retrieval correct (first token 344 s, about 728 tok/s prefill, 39.6 tok/s decode at that depth). Four ~240k prompts at once: all four correct, 43.4 tok/s in total while all four decode, about 10.9 tok/s per stream; 4.0 GiB free on the 3090 and 2.9 GiB on the V100. The same speed as Tiel-Coder: abliteration costs nothing, and neither reaches 40 tok/s per stream at this depth. No agent tests yet.

lcpp-nemotron35-lightning-q8-3090-v100.label: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Q8_0 · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots
lcpp-nemotron35-lightning-q8-3090-v100.note: Tested as a candidate agent backend serving four ~250k sessions at once on both cards, thinking off, power-capped. Short-benchmark rates: 131-136 tok/s decode on short prompts, first token 0.23-0.68 s; 250k retrieval correct with a 147 s first token (1,705 tok/s prefill) and 63.5 tok/s decode at that depth, the fastest long-prompt reader we have tried on these cards. Four ~240k prompts at once with 8-bit K/V: all four correct, about 18.8 tok/s per session. With 16-bit (F16) K/V: about 35 tok/s per session at ~240k and about 45 at ~120k, all correct, 7.0 GiB free on the 3090 and 6.5 GiB on the V100. Four OpenCode agents at once on that load (tests 1, 2, 7 and 1 again, temperature 0.6): every session ran without a harness error at 35-42 tok/s each while the others ran, server first token median 0.25 s, 7 GiB still free per card. Quality was the weak side: one of four clean (the first test 1); the second test 1 never handled the login, test 2 builds but its server only answers after its input closes, and the labyrinth scored 0 on the automatic checks.

lcpp-tiel35b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.label: Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots, F16 KV
lcpp-tiel35b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.note: The 4-bit file, used because the 6-bit one with four 256k slots of 16-bit (F16) K/V does not fit on both cards. Short-benchmark rates: 113.6 tok/s decode on short prompts, first token 0.38-1.35 s. Four ~240k prompts at once: all four correct, 100.9 tok/s in total while all four decode, about 25 per session; prefill about 710 tok/s, one session at a time, so the fourth waits about 24 minutes for its first token; 5.4 GiB free on the 3090 and 4.7 GiB on the V100. Faster than the 6-bit file with 8-bit K/V (about 11 per session), slower than Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (about 35).

lcpp-thinkingcap27b-heretic-q4km-3090-v1.label: ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B Heretic Q4_K_M (uncensored) · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots
lcpp-thinkingcap27b-heretic-q4km-3090-v1.note: Tried as a candidate agent backend with four 256k slots of 8-bit K/V across both cards: it does not fit. lcpp-flint40b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.label: Flint Preview 40B-A2.5B UD-Q4_K_XL · llama.cpp (Clover 4838ffb), RTX 3090 + V100, four 256k slots
lcpp-flint40b-udq4kxl-3090-v100.note: Tried as a candidate agent backend serving four ~250k sessions at once on both cards, with 8-bit K/V and thinking on (it is not competent with thinking off: 7 x 8 = 28). Short-benchmark rates: 87-90 tok/s decode on one short prompt, first token 0.13-0.88 s. It fits (5.5 GiB free on the 3090, 3.3 GiB on the V100) but fails on recall: the 250k retrieval reply falls into a repetition loop, and with four ~240k prompts at once every reply ran to the 6,000-token cap with all four markers wrong, at about 7 tok/s per session. tests.name: Ticket fixes in Rust
tests.what: Fix three tickets in a known-good Rust MCP server.
tests.graded: Hidden black-box checks run against the built server, plus its 155 existing tests; a claim of 'done' that fails the checks is counted.

tests.name: The labyrinth
tests.what: Write a seeded generator for a three-floor labyrinth meeting ten rules.
tests.graded: Ten unseen seeds, each in its own container, must give ten different mazes that pass the checker; walkability and honest notes are judged by hand.

tests.name: Pagoda and orrery as agent tasks
tests.what: Tests 5 and 6 solved by an agent with a sealed browser.
tests.graded: Same rubrics as tests 5 and 6, from offline renders of the file the agent leaves; two-hour cap.

tests.name: Surprising pagoda
tests.what: Build one pagoda page in steps: the scene, a surprise, then a trace of that surprise.
tests.graded: Two equal halves, each 0 to 10. Pagoda uses the test 6 scene criteria. Workflow is scored from the map: how the work was split and ordered, and whether it stopped for a person.

timeline.title: GLM-5.3-Flash runs on Maya
timeline.what: Two engine patches lift decode from 4 to 19 tok/s; tests 1 and 2 both pass.
timeline.why: Can a large model work on one card?

timeline.title: Maker sampling and a loop guard
timeline.what: Entries serve the maker's recommended sampling, and the agent stops when it repeats itself.
timeline.why: Loops had ruined several runs.

timeline.title: Graders audited, all old runs regraded
timeline.what: 125 archived runs rechecked; four test-1 verdicts changed and some test counts were corrected.
timeline.why: Old and new scores must compare.

timeline.title: Old PCIe share doubles Flash-Next on Strata
timeline.what: Restoring the old PCIe share lifts long-answer decode from 48 to 95 tok/s.
timeline.why: A newer default had halved speed.

timeline.title: Test 4: ticket fixes in Rust
timeline.what: Tiel Coder fixed three tickets, three runs each, on a crate with 155 passing tests.
timeline.why: Tests 1 and 2 never touch existing code.

timeline.title: Engine shoot-out on Qwen3.8-27B
timeline.what: TensorFold, exllamav3 and llama.cpp compared with and without drafting on one 3090.
timeline.why: Pick the fastest stack for the daily model.

timeline.title: Tests 7 and 8 added
timeline.what: Test 7 is a seeded labyrinth generator; test 8 gives the pagoda and orrery to an agent.
timeline.why: Measure design work, not only code.

timeline.title: Agent window margin changed
timeline.what: At 150k served, the agent now compacts at 89,328 tokens (60%), up from 71,000 (47%).
timeline.why: Fewer compactions, longer runs.

timeline.title: Night search for speed at 141k context
timeline.what: Four stacks timed on code at 141k tokens; Gemma-4-26B-A4B kept 123 tok/s.
timeline.why: Find what stays fast with a long history.

timeline.title: Public model-research update; LFM2.5 and Saluki tested
timeline.what: LFM2.5-24B (five quants) and a 2-bit Qwen3.8-27B tune went through tests 1 and 2.
timeline.why: Check small and very low-bit models.

timeline.title: Strata 0.1.44.1, Maya 1.1.11, exllamav3 1.6.2
timeline.what: Strata cut load time and doubled decode in the A/B; Maya fixed split digits; exllamav3 matched.
timeline.why: Re-measure each engine before changing defaults.

timeline.title: First graded test 8 batches
timeline.what: Six models that drew blank one-shot pagodas scored 7 to 10 as agents.
timeline.why: Show what tools and a browser add.

timeline.title: llama.cpp 0.7.0 replaces 0.6.0 in the router
timeline.what: Version 0.7.0 adds a GPU cache for experts and an option to keep all experts in RAM.
timeline.why: Big mixture models need that cache.

timeline.title: Gyro-S quant on Strata 0.2
timeline.what: A 1-bit-class Flash-Next quant with an MTP draft decodes 119 tok/s and passes test 2 in 24 minutes.
timeline.why: Long agent runs at 20 tok/s are too slow.

timeline.title: Expert cache, Strata 0.2.2, Flint and tqLLM
timeline.what: Flash-Next sped up on llama.cpp and Strata; a new MoE and a new engine were tried.
timeline.why: Make the 125B model usable on one card.

timeline.title: Ornith 122B and Defiance pass tests 1 and 2
timeline.what: Ornith at 13.4 tok/s and Defiance at 32.5 tok/s both cleared the CLI checks and the Rust server tests.
timeline.why: Do the new large and uncensored quants finish a real task?

timeline.title: Heretic 2 passes the code tests
timeline.what: Five CLI checks, a 7-tool server with 34 passing tests, and three maintenance tickets. Both one-shots scored 0.
timeline.why: An abliterated Flash-Next quant had not been graded on this matrix.

timeline.title: A trust run whose tests did not compile
timeline.what: Orca uncensored passed test 1, plain test 2, and three test-4 tickets. Its trust run's tests failed to compile, so 0 and 0 is not a pass.
timeline.why: A green protocol line can hide a broken test build.

timeline.title: GPU unlock speeds long prefill
timeline.what: On our 3090 box, vLLM Qwen3.8-27B long-prompt prefill rose from 736 to about 1050 tok/s. Short decode stayed near 127 tok/s.
timeline.why: Does unlocking the GPU clock help a model that already fits on the card?

timeline.title: DeepSeek Maya-XS passes the agent tests
timeline.what: On Maya 1.1.28, both rounds passed tests 1, 2 and 3. Round 1 also passed the planted-docs run and all three test-4 tickets.
timeline.why: Can a DeepSeek flash pack do the agent work on one GPU?

timeline.title: DeepSeek one-shots, scored two ways in round 1
timeline.what: Round 1 is 7 of 10 and 10 of 10 on the final code block, and 0 on the harness packaging of the same replies. Round 2 is 9 of 10 and 10 of 10 on the file as delivered.
timeline.why: Does the picture hold when the reply is a single file?

timeline.title: DeepSeek keeps two sessions apart
timeline.what: UD-IQ1_S at 6 GPU layers decodes a 252k prompt at 3.09 tok/s. Nonce isolation was at about 8.8k tokens per session; 96k is the decode depth only.
timeline.why: A long cache has to survive a reload, and a second session must not leak into the first.

timeline.title: One graded round on the backlog
timeline.what: Tiel t06 7/8, Gemma on llama.cpp 2/8, OrcaSAQ 8/8, unpruned Flash-Next 8/8, Swift 6/8, Defiance 8/8, Qwopus 8/8 on two setups.
timeline.why: The public notes had stopped on 27 October.

timeline.title: Six Flash-Next quants, story draft only
timeline.what: Partial, one round, no hand grade. Draft decode runs from 28.8 to 104.2 tok/s. Two draft legs look anomalous. A second story round is queued for all six; rank none before it.
timeline.why: The edit speed is inflated by copying the draft.

timeline.title: Two cards: a 3090 and a V100
timeline.what: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash UD-IQ1_S spans both cards: 9.7 to 16.5 tok/s short-benchmark decode, 90k retrieval correct at 96k with the first token in 22 min (was 48.5). Qwopus 27B Q6_K runs on the V100 alone at 27 tok/s.
timeline.why: A second, larger card makes room for the expert cache and long context.

timeline.title: Unsloth v3.1 quants graded
timeline.what: Four quants, one round: all pass tests 3 and 4; UD-IQ1_M is fastest and draws best; one-shot pagodas all blank.
timeline.why: Alex expected the small quants to brute-force code but draw worse; the code half held, the art half did not.

timeline.title: Flash-Next toward 150 tok/s on one 3090
timeline.what: Strata 0.2.12: 98.8 to 128.6 tok/s short-benchmark decode (350 W, English draft vocabulary, stream draft-head norm, draft min-p 0.6); 120k prompts prefill at about 2,990 tok/s; adaptive fetch keeps decode at 124-127 tok/s right after a 120k prompt on the 3090 alone; four 128k slots with the V100 keep 109 tok/s per stream. Twenty more single-change runs did not beat it; UD-Q2_K_XL reaches 123.0 and UD-Q3_K_XL 112.0 on the same setup. A memory lock, Strata 0.2.13 and llamAmpere 0.6.3.8 changed nothing. On code and JSON the goal is met: a DFlash2 draft model on UD-Q2_K_XL gives 162 tok/s on code and 203 on JSON with the quality check passing; four streams together reach only about 125 tok/s on Strata, against 165 on llama.cpp; with a 3,072 MiB VRAM reserve four 30k slots (122.7 tok/s total) and two 100k slots (103.1 tok/s total) fit the 1.5 GiB rule.
timeline.why: Goal: 150 tok/s decode and 1,000+ tok/s prefill on a larger quant. Prefill is met; code and JSON decode are met; prose decode is at 86%, limited by the draft head.

timeline.title: Agent serving profile on one 3090
timeline.what: Two 256k slots with a 20k K/V window in VRAM and a host-RAM session cache: parked 155k sessions come back in 1.25 s, four 120k streams fit at 95.8 tok/s total, and two OpenCode agents ran at once with test 2 passing.
timeline.why: Alex wanted two large agent sessions served from the 3090 without re-reading long sessions on every switch.

findings.title: Strata 0.2.2 is 17% faster than 0.2.0
findings.summary: Same-day control on the Gyro-S build with an MTP draft: code decode rose from 121.6 to 144.1 tok/s, prose from 106.4 to 123.4.
findings.quality: Tool call and needle probes passed on both builds.
findings.caveat: One load per engine; no agent run on 0.2.2 yet.

findings.summary: Flint (39.8B total, about 2.5B active, Apache-2.0) at Q3_K_XL runs entirely on the GPU at 262k context with q8 KV.

findings.quality: Not graded: no test has been run, and its one-shots are ungraded.
findings.caveat: Needs llama.cpp b11803 or newer; f16 KV does not fit. Q4_K_XL slows from 81 to 64 tok/s as more experts move to RAM.

findings.title: tqLLM serves Flash-Next fast but not for agents
findings.summary: tqLLM 1.2.3 decodes Flash-Next about 2.5x faster than llama.cpp on the same GGUF, but one prefill out-of-memory leaves every later request failing until a restart.
findings.quality: Tool calls and a 30k needle passed at 32k; at 262k with 8k prefill chunks it found a needle in 248k tokens. At 131072 context it failed on a 289-token prompt, and every later request failed until a restart.
findings.caveat: Short replies with thinking off; any prompt of 256+ tokens can trigger the failure. First load took 23 minutes cold.

findings.title: Stock SGLang now serves Flash-Next to 11 of 11 sessions
findings.summary: Three stock SGLang builds of Flash-Next, 204,800 context and two slots, all passed the multi-session probe and needles at 100k, 150k and 190k.
findings.quality: Needles found at 100k, 150k and 190k; prefill about 2,600 tok/s.
findings.caveat: The phased build was dropped; no agent test was run on these builds in this round.

findings.title: Ornith-1.5-122B reaches 16 tok/s on one card
findings.summary: A 122B Qwen3.5 mixture (8 of 256 experts per token) at UD-Q4_K_XL with 262k context and q8 KV, sweeping how many expert layers stay on the CPU.
findings.quality: Deep-prompt decode 15.8 tok/s at 40 layers; larger batches lift prefill from 118 to 392 tok/s.
findings.caveat: Not graded: one-shots ran at about 15 tok/s but were not scored, and no test has been run.

findings.title: Gyro-S + MTP: a competent 24-minute test-2 run
findings.summary: Flash-Next in Gyro-S (TQ1_0) on Strata 0.2.0-beta with an MTP draft decodes 119 tok/s on code, passes test 2 in full and scores 9 of 10 on the agent pagoda.
findings.quality: Test 2: 6 tools, 108 tests, none failing; tool call, needles at 16k and 64k and the test-1 smoke all passed.
findings.caveat: One run. The comparison arm is the IQ3_S quant on the same engine; Strata 0.2.0 was in beta.

findings.title: Tools and a browser rescue blank pagodas
findings.summary: Six models whose one-shot pagoda was blank scored 7 to 10 once they ran as agents with a sealed browser.
findings.quality: Same rubric and offline renders for both; the six are Coder 390, ThinkingCap, Orcarouter, Abliterated s1.5, Cyber and Cyber Q5.
findings.caveat: One agent run per model; orrery results are mixed (0 to 10) and some test-8 runs are not graded yet.

findings.title: Maya 1.1.11 fixes split digits and speeds up
findings.summary: On the same GLM-5.3-Flash pack, Maya 1.1.11 copied all 12 digit strings exactly and found both needles; 1.0.4 split one string and found one needle.
findings.quality: Maya-S and Maya-M on 1.1.13 also scored 12 of 12 with both needles.
findings.caveat: Two rounds per version.

findings.title: exllamav3 1.6.2 matches 1.6.1
findings.summary: The DFlash2 build of Qwen3.8-27B on exllamav3 1.6.2 decodes as fast as on 1.6.1 and finds the needle at 128k, 112k and 94k.
findings.quality: Needle 48213-KESTREL found at all three windows.
findings.caveat: Two rounds each; the difference is within noise.

findings.title: Saluki: a 2-bit Qwen3.8-27B that still calls tools
findings.summary: A 2-bit tune of Qwen3.8-27B (7.9 GB) passed test 1 with 72 tests and part-passed test 2, with 17 tools.
findings.quality: Graded by the standard test 1 and test 2 graders.
findings.caveat: Test 2 was partial (166 minutes at 22.0 tok/s); one run each.

findings.title: LFM2.5-24B is fast but passes no test 2
findings.summary: Five quants of LFM2.5-24B decoded at 125 to 176 tok/s on test 1 and passed it in three of five; none passed test 2.
findings.quality: Graded by the standard graders; test-2 servers had 0 to 3 tools.
findings.caveat: Test-1 runs were often two minutes long, so the test counts are small.

findings.title: Strata 0.1.44.1 doubles decode
findings.summary: Flash-Next on Strata, two rounds each: 0.1.44.1 loaded in a mean 60 s against 214 s, and decoded 44.9 tok/s against 18.3.
findings.quality: Same prompts and engine settings in all rounds.
findings.caveat: The first 0.1.42 round was cold; its warm round decoded 23.5 tok/s, so the true gain is nearer 1.9 times. Load time: 60 s against 214 s on the round mean, but the warm 0.1.42 round loaded in 41.5 s.

findings.title: Thinking models fail the one-shot pagoda
findings.summary: Qwen3.8-27B on vLLM with thinking on ran out of length in seven tries; with thinking off the three pages were blank.
findings.quality: Identical blank pages in the thinking-off tries.
findings.caveat: Other stacks also scored 0 on some tries: Tiel Coder one of five, Gemma-4-26B-A4B one of five, exllamav3 MTP five of six.

findings.title: Speed at 141k context
findings.summary: Four stacks timed on code with a 141k-token history: Gemma-4-26B-A4B with an MTP draft stays fastest, though it loses the most (54 %).
findings.quality: Needle found at 141k by all four.

findings.title: Flash-Next on one 3090: 129 tok/s, and 127 tok/s right after a 120k prompt
findings.summary: Toward a goal of 150 tok/s decode and 1,000+ tok/s prefill on a larger Unsloth v3.1 quant of Flash-Next, Strata 0.2.12 on one RTX 3090 reached 128.6 tok/s short-benchmark decode on UD-IQ3_XXS (from 98.8): power 250 to 350 W gave +13%, an English and code draft vocabulary +2%, and a per-token (stream) draft-head norm with a draft min-p of 0.6 most of the rest, by raising draft acceptance from about 55% to 60-68%. Prefill is met: with a K/V cache that grows with the context, a 120,007-token retrieval was correct with the first token in 40.2 s (2,987 tok/s). Strata's adaptive fetch (margin 0, PCIe share 0.55) holds 124-127 tok/s right after that long prompt on the 3090 alone. With the V100 as a peer tier that computes its cached experts, decode stays at 119 tok/s after a 30k prompt and 128 after 120k, and four 128k slots keep 109 tok/s per stream. Twenty more single-change runs found nothing faster: CPU pool and thread placement, prompt chunk size, a high-priority graph stream and a DFlash2 draft model (7.5% slower on our prose prompts) all tied or lost, and two replicates (127.6, 127.7) confirm the 128.6 base. The same setup gives 123.0 tok/s on UD-Q2_K_XL and 112.0 on UD-Q3_K_XL. On the peer tier the quant barely matters: Q2_K_XL ties IQ3_XXS at 107 tok/s. Locking Strata's PLE table in RAM is neutral (122.5 on the 3090 alone, 104-110 on the peer-tier setups, all within noise), Strata 0.2.13 ties 0.2.12 (126.1 tok/s on the 3090 alone, 109.4 on the peer tier), and llamAmpere 0.6.3.8 ties 0.6.3.2 (85.1 tok/s).

findings.title: A host-RAM session cache makes switching between long sessions 37 times faster; two 256k agent slots fit on one 3090
findings.summary: Daily driver (UD-Q2_K_XL, MTP draft head, one 3090 at 300 W), short-benchmark rates. With a 12 GiB session cache in host RAM, returning to a 93k-token session that another one displaced gives its first token in 0.93 s median instead of 34.8 s, because 99.9% of the prompt is reused; it costs 2-2.8 GiB of host RAM per parked session and no VRAM. Batch slots alone do not keep sessions (35.9 s). For agent serving, two 256k slots with two ~240k prompts at once fit on every setup tried with at least 2.1 GiB free per card. Keeping the whole K/V in 3090 VRAM starves the expert cache (51.5 tok/s total); keeping 20,480 cells per layer in VRAM and the rest in pinned host RAM gives 90.2 tok/s total with the fastest second prompt (first token 235 s). Adding the V100, as a peer tier or a layer split, gives 94-101 tok/s, one sample each, so all of these are one band.

findings.title: Flash-Next on the 3090 passes two OpenCode agents at once at 256k; a Cyber 27B fits four ~90k sessions on the V100 alone, slowly
findings.summary: Alex now wants two separate backends: a smart model on the 3090 with system RAM, and an uncensored Cyber model fully on the V100 with four sessions and as much context as practical. Smart lane: Flash-Next UD-Q2_0 on the 3090 alone (two 256k slots, 8-bit K/V, a 28 GiB session cache in host RAM, never disk) ran OpenCode test 1 and test 2 at the same time with thinking on. Test 1 passes all five live checks with 17 subcommands (our grader could not import its own test suite, so its tests are not counted); test 2 builds, exposes 9 tools, returns recorded data and passes 168 of its own tests. Both finished on their own inside the time caps: 64 and 71 minutes, 37.6 and 50.5 tok/s agent-run (48.1 and 57.3 tok/s decode), first token median 0.94 and 0.74 s, largest prompts about 189k and 217k tokens. A parked 189k-token session came back from host RAM with its first token in 0.89 s. Cyber lane, short benchmarks on the V100 alone: Qwen3.8-27B Cyber Q5_K_M fits four 64k slots (2.2 GiB free) and four 72k (1.0 GiB free) but not four 80k; the IQ4_XS quant fits four 96k slots (2.7 GiB free; four 112k loads and answers correctly but leaves only 332 MiB, under our 512 MiB floor) and is faster (36.3 vs 28.6 tok/s on one session). With four long prompts the card reads them one at a time at about 400-490 tok/s, so the last of four ~90k prompts waits 14 minutes for its first token, and four sessions decode at about 8-9.5 tok/s each.
